architecture_strategy.reasoning: Step 03 classified one composite playbook (primary playbook; secondary process_flow and taxonomy). A linear sequence carries the six numbered steps and continues into the unnumbered downstream chain to closed-won (structure-001). Each step is a modular section holding its optional tools (structure-002/008). Step 3 is a three-group taxonomy (structure-003), Step 6 is two parallel lanes (structure-004), Step 4 pairs an ordered stage list with peer tiers that are related but unmapped (structure-005/006), and Step 5 is a hub that Steps 1–4 inform and that supports Step 6 (structure-007). Explicit connectors are reserved for sequence. Information flow into the CRM is required but flexible in presentation and is not treated as an execution dependency. Membership uses containment, and tools use supporting associations, to avoid connector clutter. Workflow, funnel, decision-tree and ecosystem patterns stay rejected as in Step 03.

layout_requirements.requirement: Steps 1–6 read as one directional numbered sequence; Step 6 continues into the downstream chain.

Downstream items continue the flow but stay unnumbered and distinct from steps; closed-won is the single terminal element; no closed-lost branch; no direct links from individual demand-generation activities to closed-won.
Tools are subordinate to the step or activity they belong to, never process stages; repeated tools appear in every step that uses them.
Step 3 holds three sibling sub-groups (first, second, third party) with all 25 categories and no vendor slots.
Step 6 shows two parallel groups, one-to-one and one-to-many; activities without tools still appear; no inbound/outbound framing.
Step 4 places ordered awareness stages and peer tiers side by side with no connector or alignment implying a stage-to-tier mapping; no numeric scores.
Step 5 reads as a hub: one grouped cue that Steps 1–4 inform CRM records, and an onward link to Step 6; HubSpot and Salesforce shown as either/or.
The optionality note sits with the title and visibly governs every tool cluster.
Allocate the most space to Step 3 (very high density), then Step 6.
Exact placement of steps (strictly linear vs wrapped or hub-centred) is free as long as numbered order stays legible.

representation_constraints.statement: Present every tool/platform as an optional alternative; never as a required stack or recommendation to use all.
Repeat a tool in each step it belongs to (e.g. Ocean.io in Steps 1 and 2); do not deduplicate across steps.
Do not invent tool or vendor names; signal categories and parallel dialing / gifting remain without vendors.
Number exactly six steps; downstream items and closed-won are unnumbered.
Show only the path toward closed-won; no closed-lost branch.
No numerical scores or thresholds; no mapping between awareness stages and tiers.
Demand generation is one-to-one / one-to-many, not inbound/outbound; video outreach sits in one-to-many.
Use corrected orders: considering before selecting; sequence enrollment before CRM tasks; recap order for steps.
Use Claygent (not Clay) in Step 2, Claude Code (not Claude), and X (formerly Twitter).
Do not show excluded items as active content: Apollo, Pipedrive, Reddit ads, email opens as a category; website visits only under first-party.
HubSpot and Salesforce are either/or CRM options, not both required.
